chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Any believer who goes out to visit his brother, recognizing his right, Allah writes for him a good deed for every step, erases a bad deed from him, and raises his rank. And when he knocks on the door, the gates of heaven are opened for him.

So when they meet, shake hands, and embrace, Allah turns His face towards them, then boasts about them to the angels, saying: 'Look at My two servants who visited each other and loved each other for My sake. It is a right upon Me that I should not punish them with the Fire after this occasion.'

So when he departs, the angels escort him, in the number of his breaths, steps, and words, protecting him from the afflictions of the world and the calamities of the Hereafter, until the same time the following night.

So if he dies in the interval between them, he is excused from the reckoning. And if the visited one recognizes from the right of the visitor what the visitor recognized from the right of the visited, he will have the like of his reward.

key_terms.عَارِفاً بِحَقِّهِ: recognizing his right (acknowledging the social/spiritual dues)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and divine blessings for visiting a believer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* elevates *Ziyarat* (visitation) beyond social courtesy to a profound act of worship that secures divine favor and angelic protection. It highlights the reciprocal nature of spiritual rights, noting that if the visited party equally recognizes the visitor's rights, both share the same reward, culminating in exemption from the harshness of the Day of Judgment's reckoning.
